# Incident Report — MTA 2026-01-31 Traffic Analysis

## Evidence Reviewed
- `2026-01-31-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (51,181 frames). No IDS/Suricata alert export was present in the evidence directory — this analysis is based on raw packet capture only.

## Victim Host
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.1.21.58** |
| MAC address | **00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-ES9F3ML** (NetBIOS also broadcasts as `WIN11OFFICE`; domain FQDN `DESKTOP-ES9F3ML.win11office.com`) |
| Logged-in AD user | **gwyatt** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString from 10.1.21.58 to the domain controller 10.1.21.2) |

Confirmed via DHCP Request (option 12 hostname `DESKTOP-ES9F3ML`, chaddr `00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2`), NBNS registration, and ARP replies mapping 10.1.21.58 to that MAC.

## Malware Family and Attribution
**Behavioral attribution, not signature-confirmed** — there is no AV/IDS/YARA hit in this evidence set, so the family name below is based on distinctive C2 protocol traits observed in traffic, not a matched signature.

The traffic is consistent with an **infostealer delivered through a fingerprint-gated Traffic Distribution System (TDS) / fake-download chain**, with a C2 checkin pattern matching the "StealC"-style panel API (`/api/set_agent` with `id`/`token`/`agent`/`act=log` parameters, JS-based browser fingerprinting gate before payload delivery). Key behavioral evidence:

1. **Fake file-host delivery chain** (t≈45–48s): `hiyter.com` → `media.megafilehub4.lat` → `arch.filemegahab4.sbs`, culminating in a ~16 MB payload transfer from **104.21.46.67** (SNI hidden behind Cloudflare Encrypted Client Hello — ClientHello SNI literally presents as `cloudflare-ech.com`, an evasion technique to hide the real hostname from network monitoring).
2. **Browser fingerprinting/anti-bot gate** (t≈90–103s): a served JS payload (recovered from HTTP object `set_agent?...&agent=Chrome`) harvests `navigator.*` properties, WebGL renderer/vendor, canvas fingerprint, WebRTC candidates, audio fingerprint, and installed plugins, then POSTs the result back with `&act=log`. The script contains a Russian-language code comment (`// Преобразуем в URLSearchParams`), indicating Russian-speaking tooling authorship consistent with known Eastern-European stealer/TDS crimeware.
3. Registration/check-in used a persistent bot `id` and build `token`, re-sent once per browser identified on the host (`agent=Chrome`, then `agent=Edge`) — consistent with a stealer enumerating installed browsers to target their credential stores.

## Indicators of Compromise

### Command-and-control / malicious infrastructure (IP:port)
| IP:Port | Domain (SNI/Host) | Role |
|---|---|---|
| 153.92.1.49:80 | whitepepper.su | **Primary C2** — fingerprint/telemetry collection panel (`/api/set_agent`) |
| 104.21.46.67:443 | arch.filemegahab4.sbs (ECH-masked, presents as cloudflare-ech.com) | Payload host — ~16 MB encrypted download |
| 104.21.48.156:443 | media.megafilehub4.lat | Fake file-host / redirector |
| 62.72.32.156:443 | whooptm.cyou | Redirector / gate |
| 104.21.9.36 / 172.67.141.109:443 | communicationfirewall-security.cc | Secondary/follow-on C2 or redirector |
| 80.97.160.24:443 | holiday-forever.cc | Secondary/follow-on C2 or redirector |
| 104.21.22.231 / 172.67.207.145:443 | hiyter.com | Initial landing/entry domain |

### Malicious domains
- `hiyter.com`
- `media.megafilehub4.lat`
- `arch.filemegahab4.sbs`
- `whooptm.cyou`
- `whitepepper.su`
- `holiday-forever.cc`
- `communicationfirewall-security.cc`

### Malicious URLs (observed in cleartext HTTP)
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome&act=log` (POST, exfiltrates browser fingerprint JSON)
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge&act=log`

Bot ID: `3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C` — Build/campaign token: `842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b`

### Transferred files / hashes
No SHA256 hash or filename could be recovered from the capture. The ~16 MB payload transfer from 104.21.46.67 is entirely TLS-encrypted application data with the real SNI hidden by Encrypted Client Hello (ECH); no HTTP object could be exported from that flow. The two files that were extractable via HTTP object export (`set_agent` responses) are JS/HTML fingerprinting gate code, not the delivered malware binary — no hash is claimed for those since they are gate infrastructure, not the payload itself.

## Notes
- Traffic to the domain controller (10.1.21.2 — LDAP/Kerberos/DRSUAPI/CLDAP) reflects normal domain-joined workstation behavior and shows no signs of lateral movement or DCSync abuse in this capture.
- Attribution above should be treated as behavioral pattern-matching against known stealer/TDS tradecraft (fingerprint gate → encrypted payload → periodic `set_agent` beaconing), not a confirmed family name — validate with endpoint/AV telemetry from host DESKTOP-ES9F3ML if available.
